description: Cross-binding conformance for build-time value invention over a `kind: "derived"` index set (esm-spec §4.2, §9.6.6; issue #266). A `distinct` faq under `bool_and_or` with a `skolem` key, exposed via `from_faq`, MUST be materialized at build so a contraction over the derived axis counts its members. Before this category Rust skipped value invention for any model without an `argmin`/`argmax` op and sized the unmaterialized axis as 0, so the document validated and silently answered 0; Julia and Python refused it because they read only supplied arrays as key columns, not an unknown defined by a `const` equation. The VALUE half pins the answer 3. The REFUSAL half pins that a producer which cannot run is refused rather than contracted as empty: an absent key column MUST be refused with `derived_index_set_unmaterialized`, and a state-reading key with `relational_node_in_continuous`, which a binding MAY raise at load (structural validation) or at build. In both refusals there is no actual, and in particular not 0.

scope_excluded.go: No simulator and no inline-test runner, so this category cannot be run here. Go registers `derived_index_set_unmaterialized` for the shared vocabulary.
scope_excluded.typescript: No simulator and no inline-test runner, so this category cannot be run here. TypeScript registers `derived_index_set_unmaterialized` for the shared vocabulary.

cases.note: Four rows carry three distinct (polProcessID, engTechID) pairs; both key columns are unknowns defined by `const` equations.
`engTechID` is a shaped parameter with no data, so the producer cannot run and the contraction has no members to count.
The key reads the ODE state `u`, so the producer classifies CONTINUOUS (CONFORMANCE_SPEC §5.7 guard 2).
